newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ABN AMRO, Citibank to raise $175 mln for Romania.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO, Citibank to raise $175 mln for Romania.

text.p: Dutch ABN AMRO Bank and U.S. Citibank have launched a $175 million syndicated loan for the National Bank of Romania, the Loan Pricing Corp (LPC) reported.

The deal, expected to close on September 16, has a three- year maturity and is priced at 187.5 basis points over LIBOR, higher than the 175 basis points of the National Bank's syndication of $90 million led by Japan's Sanwa Bank in April.

The LPC said lenders have the option to call the loan at the end of the second year. Commitments of between $2.5 million and $10 million are being sought, with a top upfront fee of 40 bps offered. Banks coming in at $10 million will be designated co-arrangers.
The National Bank has authority to raise up to $1.5 billion by the end of 1996.
It has already drawn about $975 million so far, the bulk of that through Japanese Samurai bonds led by Nomura Securities and Eurobonds launched by Merrill Lynch.

Romania is rated BA-three (BA-3) by Moody's Investors Service, BB-minus (BB-) by Standard and Poor's, BB-minus (BB-) by IBCA and BB+ (BB-plus) by Japan Credit Rating Agency. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
